title: Уксус в фирменный рулет  (Vinegar in the Signature Roll)

segments.t: Left alone to place Barani's signature meat roll into the oven, Chef Barinov decides to take his revenge on his former pupil by dousing the dish with sour vinegar. Meanwhile outside in the courtyard, Senya and Fedya try to rig a prank on Barani's convertible.
А вот хрен тебе с уксусом, господин.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Then I will head out.' Notice how Russian expresses 'then' and 'go' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Vika answers right away.
'It has already started.' The meaning hinges on 'now' working together with 'started' in spoken Russian.
'We wrap all of this up.' In Russian, the idea of 'all' flows naturally into 'to wrap up' without extra filler words.
'All that is left is to put it in the oven.' Notice the reflexive suffix on the verb meaning 'was left', turning the action back on the subject. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'He wanted to buy me off in France.' The grammar packs 'France' and 'wanted' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
А вот хрен тебе с уксусом, господин.
'Well, here is horseradish with vinegar for you, mister.' Vika brings out the contrast between 'and' and 'there you go' in a few short words.
'Viktor Barinov is not for sale.' In Russian, the idea of 'Viktor' flows naturally into 'to be sold' without extra filler words. Vika answers right away.
'That is much better.' The meaning hinges on 'there you go' working together with 'better' in spoken Russian.
'Now that is really good.' Notice how Russian expresses 'there you go' and 'fine' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Well, how is it going over there?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'come on' and finishing on 'there'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Maybe we should not do this?' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'maybe' to negate the statement.
'It did not work.' Vika anchors the line on 'not', while 'to work' completes the thought.
'All the worse for him.' The grammar packs 'to him' and 'worse' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
А вот хрен тебе с уксусом, господин.
